topic: Fundamentals of Vector Spaces: Span, Dependence, and Bases

outline.topic: Fundamentals of Vector Spaces: Span, Dependence, and Bases

sections.title: Prerequisite Review: The Vector Concept
sections.content: Define a vector as a directed line segment from the origin. Visualize 2D vectors as arrows. Introduce 'Linear Combination' as scaling and adding arrows together.
sections.example: Imagine a robot arm moving in a 2D plane: scaling two basic motor inputs (v1, v2) to reach any coordinate (x, y).

sections.title: The Concept of Span: 'Reachability'
sections.content: Define Span as the set of all possible points reachable by taking linear combinations of a set of vectors. Visualize this as the 'shadow' or 'area' cast by the vectors.
sections.example: Two non-parallel vectors in 2D 'span' the entire plane; one vector only spans a single line.

sections.title: Linear Dependence: The 'Redundant' Vector
sections.content: Explain Linear Dependence: A set is dependent if one vector can be expressed as a combination of others (i.e., it doesn't add 'new' dimensions). Visualize this as a third vector lying flat on the plane formed by the first two.
sections.example: If you have three people pulling a wagon in the same direction, the third person is 'linearly dependent'—their effort doesn't change the path.

sections.title: Bases: The Minimalist Framework
sections.content: Define a Basis as the 'Goldilocks' set: enough vectors to span the space, but no redundancy (linearly independent). This acts as a coordinate system for the space.
sections.example: The standard basis vectors i=(1,0) and j=(0,1) are the most efficient 'map' for a 2D grid.

sections.title: Summary & Synthesis
sections.content: Recap the logical progression: Linear Combinations build Span; too many vectors create Dependence; the minimal set required to span is a Basis.
sections.example: Think of a basis as the 'keys' on a piano: they are independent notes that, when combined, can span the entire musical range of the instrument.

storyboard.title: Prerequisite Review: The Vector Concept
lecture_lines: Vectors are directed segments from the origin.
Scaling and adding vectors creates linear combinations.
animations: Create a labeled vector arrow from origin, colored #FF5733.
Animate the vector scaling by a factor of 2.
Rotate the vector by 45 degrees counter-clockwise.
Show vector addition using the parallelogram rule.
Highlight the resultant vector with a bright #33FF57 color.

storyboard.title: The Concept of Span: 'Reachability'
lecture_lines: Span is the set of all reachable points.
Think of it as area covered by vectors.
Vectors define what space we can reach.
animations: Visualize origin point and two vectors in 2D space.
Animate scalar multiplication of vectors filling 2D plane.
Highlight the span area with a semi-transparent #3385FF.

storyboard.title: Linear Dependence: The 'Redundant' Vector
lecture_lines: Linear dependence means one vector is redundant.
It adds no new dimensions to space.
Dependent vectors lie on existing planes.
animations: Display two vectors, one as a multiple of another.
Highlight the second vector fading away, #808080.
Show the remaining basis vector staying static, #FFFFFF.

storyboard.title: Bases: The Minimalist Framework
lecture_lines: A basis is a minimal spanning set.
It provides an efficient coordinate system.
No redundancy, yet spans the space perfectly.
animations: Display a grid of lines formed by two vectors.
Highlight the intersection points as unique coordinates.
Label the basis vectors 'i-hat' and 'j-hat' in #FFFF00.

storyboard.title: Summary & Synthesis
lecture_lines: Linear combinations build up our spanning sets.
Redundancy creates linear dependence in vectors.
Bases are the minimal set for space.
animations: Briefly summarize span concept with a recap animation.
Display linear dependence rule as a formula #FF00FF.
Show a basis forming a complete coordinate system.
